answer: Time-locked vesting: every reward an agent earns flows into a slow river of escrow that unlocks only over a 30-epoch horizon. If graders later flag any linked account as a sybil, the whole unvested balance is clawed back. A raven-flock of fake identities must fund each clone's work upfront and wait weeks to cash out, while one detection wipes every pending payout, so splitting into many identities raises risk without raising profit.
